previewProject.name: world-server-preview

schemaCompatibilityCheck.checkedVia: mcp__supabase__list_tables(verbose=true) against the actual live schema, not inferred from migration filenames

findings.requirement: public.voxel_worlds must have a 'revision' column (bigint) for the function's optimistic-concurrency CAS: `where id = p_world_id and revision = p_expected_revision`
findings.actual: public.voxel_worlds columns are: id (text), seed (bigint), settings (jsonb), created_at, updated_at. There is NO 'revision' column — 'seed' exists instead, which is unrelated.

findings.requirement: public.voxel_world_events table must exist with columns id/world_id/revision/event_type/cx/cz/radius_chunks/payload/source/created_by_user/created_by_guest/idempotency_key/event_checksum, since the function inserts into it and also selects from it for idempotency-key lookups
findings.actual: public.voxel_world_events does not exist on this project at all (not in the public schema table list).

schemaCompatibilityCheck.rootCauseOfGap: supabase/migrations/20260831072856_world_procedural_recipe_atomic_commit_v3.sql only contains `create or replace function` — it assumes voxel_worlds.revision and the whole voxel_world_events table already exist ('using existing voxel_worlds + voxel_world_events', per the migration's own comment). No migration anywhere in this repo's supabase/migrations/ directory creates voxel_world_events or adds a revision column to voxel_worlds (grepped the full migrations directory — zero other matches). Production apparently has this prerequisite schema already (per the user's own verification); this preview project does not — the two environments' base schemas have diverged, not just their applied-migration lists.
schemaCompatibilityCheck.postgresBehaviorNote: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION would very likely SUCCEED even against this incompatible schema — Postgres does not validate table/column references inside a plpgsql function body at creation time, only at first EXECUTE. Applying the migration as-is would therefore appear to succeed and then fail (or silently do the wrong thing) the first time anything actually calls the function. This is why a compatibility check against live columns, not just 'did CREATE FUNCTION return an error', was necessary.

previewProject.reasonNotApplied: Schema is incompatible (see findings above). The user's own instruction was explicit: check compatibility first, apply ONLY if compatible. It is not. Applying a NEW prerequisite migration (adding voxel_worlds.revision, creating voxel_world_events with appropriate constraints/indexes/RLS/grants) would be a real, unreviewed schema-design decision — new table, new column, new RLS policy — that was not part of what was asked, and this project already holds one live row of real data in voxel_worlds (rows:1) that a wrong backfill choice on a new NOT NULL/default column could affect. Recommending a human decision rather than inventing the prerequisite migration unilaterally.

databaseDriftStatusDetail: Production: applied and (per the user) verified — closed. Preview: migration correctly NOT applied due to a genuine, evidenced schema incompatibility (missing voxel_worlds.revision column and the entire voxel_world_events table) — open, pending a decision on how to backfill the prerequisite schema on preview, or a decision that preview does not need this feature yet.
recommendedNextStep: A human (or a follow-up session with explicit authorization) should decide: (a) author and review a prerequisite migration adding voxel_worlds.revision + creating voxel_world_events on preview, matching however production actually defines them (which this session cannot inspect), or (b) treat preview as intentionally behind on this feature for now and skip it.
